input.rationale: Of the three compositions measured, 137 (Cu0.50 Fe0.19 V0.30) had the highest photocurrent, 7.2e-7 A. That is 1.7x the Cu:V≈1:1 point and 1.9x the V-rich point. XRD shows a distinct Cu-rich vanadate-type phase (sample peaks at Q≈1.65, 2.13, 2.26, 2.49 and 3.02 Å⁻¹, besides the SnO2 substrate peaks). This fits the reduced-gap copper vanadates that absorb 2.4 eV photons.

rejected.reason: Measured 4.2e-7 A. Cu:V ~1:1 with low Fe; weak phase peaks, lower photocurrent.
Measured 3.8e-7 A. V-rich, XRD dominated by V2O5-like peaks, which is a poor photoanode.
XRD only; no merit budget left to test. Fe-rich Cu-Fe-V oxides are expected to have poor carrier transport.

content.text:
I submitted index 137 (Cu 0.50, Fe 0.19, V 0.30) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured, 7.2×10⁻⁷ A. I don't know how it compares with the best in the library, because only 3 of the 297 compositions were measured for photocurrent.

| Index | Composition (Cu / Fe / V) | Photocurrent | XRD |
|---|---|---|---|
| **137** | 0.50 / 0.19 / 0.30 | **7.2×10⁻⁷ A** | Its own set of peaks, likely a copper vanadate |
| 197 | 0.40 / 0.11 / 0.49 | 4.2×10⁻⁷ A | Only weak peaks from the film |
| 19 | 0.10 / 0.11 / 0.79 | 3.8×10⁻⁷ A | Peaks match V₂O₅, which usually works poorly as a photoanode |

- **XRD:** I used 4 of the 5 XRD scans. On each one, the peaks that repeat across all samples (around Q ≈ 1.88, 2.66 and 3.57 Å⁻¹) come from the tin-oxide (SnO₂) substrate, so I set those aside. I also scanned an iron-rich point (173), but its photocurrent was never measured.
- **How the choices were made:** I picked the three points to cover different regions (copper-rich, roughly equal copper and vanadium, and vanadium-rich), based on the XRD and on the fact that copper vanadates absorb 2.4 eV light. I meant to measure them one at a time and adjust after each result, but I sent all three at once. So none of the choices was guided by an earlier photocurrent result.
- **What was never measured:** The iron-rich region and most of the copper-rich compositions were never measured for photocurrent. A better composition could be in either area.
